newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-TOULOUSE BEAT CARDIFF IN EUROPEAN CUP FINAL REPEAT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TOULOUSE BEAT CARDIFF IN EUROPEAN CUP FINAL REPEAT.

text.p: Despite having hot-tempered hooker Patrick Soulas sent off midway through the first-half, 14-man Toulouse outclassed Cardiff 36-20 in a rematch of last season's European Cup final on Saturday.

The defending champions struggled in the first-half after losing Soulas and trailed 12-11 at half-time in their pool D match but eventually managed four tries, the first by France centre Thomas Castaignede who scored 18 points.

Cardiff had to be content with a single try scored by centre Gareth Jones with ten minutes left, plus five penalties from fly-half Lee Jarvis, who was replacing injured former national captain Jonathan Davies.
The first side definitely through to the quarter-finals, however, are Welsh club Pontypridd who scored a notable 19-6 victory over English champions Bath.
Toulouse made the classic start to a Franco-British confrontation when Castaignede, the star of last season's final, opened the scoring as early as the third minute after a brilliant run.

But the French forwards lacked discipline and Toulouse quickly found themselves a man short when Soulas was sent off for two bookings. Cardiff took full advantage with four first-half penalties through Jarvis before the tide turned against them in the second-half.

In the 51st minute, fullback Stephane Ougier went slaloming through the Welsh defence to launch Emile N'Tamack to the try-line and flanker Sylvain Dispagne then sent winger David Berty under the posts.
Berty wrapped up the match with a last-gasp try after a long run down the touchline, ensuring Toulouse now have the only 100 per cent record in their competitive pool.
Bath were undone by a fired-up Pontypridd side in wet conditions, losing the forward battle and looking short of inspiration in the absence of Jeremy Guscott, Phil de Glanville and Henry Paul.

The Welsh cupholders scored the game's only try through scrum-half Paul John and 14 points from the boot of Neil Jenkins completed the job. Bath now have to beat Dax of France at home next weekend to keep alive their qualification chances.

Pau, who scored 13 tries in their only previous match against Scottish Borders, were brought back to earth by Llanelli in Wales. They lost 31-15 with New Zealander Frano Botica contributing 16 points.
